title: List departments — loaded state, company scope, no raw uid visible
preconditions: User has HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW permission. At least 1 department exists for the selected company.
steps:
1. Log in as a user with HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW.
2. Navigate to /admin/hr/departments.
3. Select the company from the company selector.
4. Wait for the table to render.
testData: Department code: HR, name: Human Resources
expected: Table lists departments with code and name. No raw uid is visible in any cell. ApiResponse envelope is unwrapped by the interceptor so the component receives List<DepartmentDto> directly.

title: Departments list — forbidden state for user without HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW
preconditions: A user with NO HR permissions exists.
steps:
1. Log in as the no-permission user.
2. Confirm the HR & Payroll nav group or the Departments nav item is not rendered.
3. Attempt to navigate directly to /admin/hr/departments.
4. Confirm the route guard redirects or shows the forbidden state.
expected: Nav item hidden. Direct navigation blocked by route guard (requirePermission('HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW')). HTTP GET /api/v1/hr/departments returns 403.

title: Create department — valid; VIEW-only user sees 403
preconditions: User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE. A company is selected.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/departments.
2. Click New Department.
3. Enter code FIN and name Finance.
4. Save.
5. Repeat step 2-4 logged in as a VIEW-only user and verify the create control is hidden and a direct POST returns 403.
expected: 201 Created. DepartmentDto returned with code FIN and name Finance. Row appears in the list. VIEW-only user: New Department button absent; direct POST returns 403.

title: Deactivate department — soft-delete, unknown uid returns 404
preconditions: Department FIN created in HR-003. User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. From the departments list, find the Finance department.
2. Choose Deactivate and confirm.
3. Verify the department is marked inactive (soft-delete).
4. Attempt to deactivate an unknown uid via the API and verify 404.
expected: 204 No Content. Department record is deactivated (status flag), not hard-deleted. Unknown uid returns 404. VIEW-only user attempting the action gets 403.

title: Employees list — pagination meta correct, no uid in cells
preconditions: At least 21 employees exist in the company so there are at least 2 pages at size 20. User has HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/employees.
2. Observe the table renders with employee number, name, department name, and status.
3. Use the paginator controls (FIRST, PREVIOUS, page numbers, NEXT, LAST) to navigate.
4. Verify meta fields: page, size, totalElements, totalPages, hasNext.
expected: Page 1 shows 20 rows. Paginator is visible. No raw uid in any cell. Meta totalPages >= 2 and hasNext = true on page 1. Navigating pages refetches correctly.

title: Create employee — minimal required fields; server generates employee number
preconditions: User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE. At least 1 department exists.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/employees and click New Employee.
2. Fill firstName: Asha, lastName: Mussa, hireDate: 2026-01-15.
3. Pick department Finance by name (not by uid).
4. Leave all optional fields blank.
5. Save.
6. Confirm the success notification shows the employee number.
testData: firstName: Asha, lastName: Mussa, hireDate: 2026-01-15, department: Finance
expected: 201 Created. EmployeeDto returned with server-generated employeeNumber (EMP-000001 format) and status ACTIVE. Row appears in list. Department shown by name, not uid.

title: Create employee — blank required fields rejected client and server side
preconditions: User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the New Employee form.
2. Leave firstName blank and attempt to save.
3. Observe client-side validation message.
4. Bypass client validation and send a POST without firstName.
5. Observe server-side 400 response.
expected: Client validation shows 'First name is required.' without sending the POST. If bypassed, server returns 400 with @NotBlank error on firstName. Same for missing lastName and hireDate.

title: Archive employee — ACTIVE transitions to TERMINATED; ON_LEAVE and SUSPENDED are not settable via UI
preconditions: An ACTIVE employee exists. User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the employee detail at /admin/hr/employees/uid/:uid.
2. Click Archive and confirm.
3. Verify the status badge changes to TERMINATED.
4. Confirm the employee record is retained (soft-delete).
5. Verify there is no button or endpoint accessible via the UI to set ON_LEAVE or SUSPENDED.
expected: 204 returned. Employee status = TERMINATED. Record still exists in the database. No UI affordance to set ON_LEAVE or SUSPENDED (those enum values have no controller endpoint in this domain).

title: Multi-tenant isolation — tenant A cannot access tenant B employees
preconditions: Two companies (tenant A and tenant B) each have employees. User is an HR manager of tenant A only.
steps:
1. Log in as tenant-A HR manager.
2. List employees — confirm only tenant A employees appear.
3. Attempt to fetch a tenant-B employee uid directly via GET /api/v1/hr/employees/uid/{B-uid}.
4. Attempt list with companyId of tenant B.
testData: Tenant A companyId, Tenant B employee uid
expected: Tenant B employees never appear in the list. Direct B-uid fetch returns 403 (ScopeGuard.assertCanActIn). List with tenant-B companyId returns 403.

title: Create PERMANENT contract — currency forced TZS, payFrequency defaults MONTHLY
preconditions: Employee with no active contract. User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/contracts.
2. Pick the employee by name using the uid-picker.
3. Choose contract type PERMANENT.
4. Enter baseSalary 1500000, startDate 2026-01-01.
5. Set statutory checkboxes: payeResident on, nssfMember on.
6. Save.
expected: 201 Created. ContractDto with currency TZS, payFrequency MONTHLY, active = true. Employee picker showed name not uid.

title: Duplicate active contract rejected with 409
preconditions: Employee already has an active contract (HR-010). User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Attempt to create a second contract for the same employee who already has an active one.
2. Observe the error response.
expected: 409 ConflictException with message 'Employee already has an active contract.' No second contract created.

title: Create FIXED_TERM contract with end date; CASUAL and PROBATION types
preconditions: Three employees each with no active contract. User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Create FIXED_TERM contract for employee 1 with start 2026-02-01 and end 2026-12-31, baseSalary 900000.
2. Create CASUAL contract for employee 2.
3. Create PROBATION contract for employee 3.
4. Verify each ContractDto echoes the correct contractType.
testData: FIXED_TERM: start 2026-02-01, end 2026-12-31, baseSalary 900000; CASUAL and PROBATION with respective employees
expected: All three contracts created with the correct contractType. FIXED_TERM retains the end date. Currency TZS in all cases.

title: Terminate contract — active flag flips to false; new contract can then be created
preconditions: Employee with one active contract. User has HR.EMPLOYEE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. From the contracts panel for the employee, click Terminate and confirm.
2. Verify 204 returned and active = false.
3. Create a new contract for the same employee — verify it succeeds (no more active-contract conflict).
expected: 204 No Content. Contract active = false (boolean toggle, no separate status enum for contracts). New contract creation subsequently succeeds with 201.

title: Submit leave request — status PENDING; missing required fields rejected
preconditions: An employee exists. A LeaveType is seeded directly in the DB (no UI endpoint). User has HR.LEAVE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/leave-requests.
2. Pick the employee by name.
3. Enter leaveTypeId (seeded Annual Leave id), fromDate 2026-03-10, toDate 2026-03-14, days 5, reason Family.
4. Submit.
5. Also try submitting with days = 0 and verify 400.
testData: leaveTypeId: seeded Annual Leave id, from: 2026-03-10, to: 2026-03-14, days: 5, reason: Family
expected: 201 Created. LeaveRequestDto with status PENDING, employeeName and leaveTypeName resolved. days = 0 returns 400 (@Positive). Missing required fields (leaveTypeId, fromDate, toDate, days) each return 400.

title: Approve leave request — PENDING to APPROVED; MANAGE-only user denied approve
preconditions: A PENDING leave request exists (HR-014). Two users: one with HR.LEAVE.APPROVE, one with HR.LEAVE.MANAGE only.
steps:
1. Log in as the HR.LEAVE.APPROVE user.
2. Open the leave request detail at /admin/hr/leave-requests/uid/:uid.
3. Choose Approve, enter note OK, submit.
4. Verify status = APPROVED and decidedBy/decidedAt are stamped.
5. Log in as MANAGE-only user and attempt to approve — verify 403.
expected: Status changes to APPROVED. decidedBy and decidedAt fields populated. MANAGE-only user attempting approve returns 403.

title: Reject leave request; illegal decision values PENDING and CANCELLED return 400
preconditions: A PENDING leave request exists. User has HR.LEAVE.APPROVE.
steps:
1. Open the leave request detail.
2. Choose Reject with note 'Coverage gap' and submit.
3. Verify status = REJECTED.
4. Open a second PENDING request and attempt decide with decision = PENDING.
5. Attempt decide with decision = CANCELLED.
testData: decision: REJECTED, note: Coverage gap; then PENDING and CANCELLED as invalid values
expected: REJECTED decision succeeds — status REJECTED, decidedBy/At set. decision = PENDING returns 400 with 'Decision must be APPROVED or REJECTED.' decision = CANCELLED returns the same 400. Status remains PENDING in both invalid cases.

title: Create loan — principal, installment, GL account via picker; currency defaults TZS
preconditions: An employee and a GL account exist. User has HR.LOAN.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/loans.
2. Pick the employee by name.
3. Enter principal 600000, installment 100000, startDate 2026-02-01.
4. Pick the GL account by name (not by uid).
5. Leave currency blank.
6. Save.
expected: 201 Created. EmployeeLoanDto with server-generated loanNumber, outstandingAmount = 600000, currency TZS (defaulted). GL account shown by name not uid.

title: Approve loan — status changes to ACTIVE; no close/settle/cancel endpoint via UI
preconditions: A loan exists in its initial state (HR-017). User has HR.LOAN.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the loan detail at /admin/hr/loans/uid/:uid.
2. Click Approve.
3. Verify status = ACTIVE.
4. Confirm there is no UI control to set SETTLED or CANCELLED (close is backend-only, no controller endpoint).
expected: status = ACTIVE after approve. No Settle or Cancel buttons present in the UI (those states have no controller endpoint in this domain).

title: Loan deduction flows into payroll — installment deducted; min(installment, outstanding) rule
preconditions: ACTIVE loan with outstanding > 0 for an employee with an active contract. A payroll run in DRAFT status. User has HR.LOAN.MANAGE and HR.PAYROLL.RUN.
steps:
1. Confirm the loan is ACTIVE with outstanding 600000 and installment 100000.
2. Calculate the payroll run for the period.
3. Open the payroll lines tab and find the employee.
4. Verify a DEDUCTION line 'Loan Repayment: <loanNumber>' of 100000 exists.
5. Create a second loan where installment exceeds outstanding — verify only the remaining outstanding is deducted.
testData: Loan: outstanding 600000, installment 100000; edge: outstanding 50000, installment 100000 → deduction should be 50000
expected: Normal case: deduction = 100000. Edge case: deduction = 50000 (min applied). Net salary reduced by the deduction amount.

title: Create EARNING FIXED taxable pensionable pay component; GL account via picker
preconditions: A GL account exists. User has HR.PAYCOMPONENT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/pay-components.
2. Click New Component.
3. Enter code HOUSING, name Housing Allowance.
4. Choose kind EARNING, basis FIXED.
5. Check taxable and pensionable.
6. Pick the GL account by name.
7. Save.
testData: code: HOUSING, name: Housing Allowance, kind: EARNING, basis: FIXED, taxable: true, pensionable: true
expected: 201 Created. PayComponentDto with the chosen kind/basis/flags and active = true. Blank code or name returns 400. Null kind/basis/glAccountId returns 400.

title: Create DEDUCTION FIXED non-taxable component; deactivate via soft-delete
preconditions: A GL account exists. User has HR.PAYCOMPONENT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Create a DEDUCTION component with code UNION, name Union Dues, basis FIXED, taxable false, pensionable false.
2. Verify 201 and kind = DEDUCTION.
3. Open the component detail.
4. Rename it, save — verify updated name.
5. Click Deactivate — verify 204 and active = false (soft-delete).
testData: code: UNION, name: Union Dues, kind: DEDUCTION, basis: FIXED
expected: 201 on create. Rename persists. Deactivate returns 204 and sets active = false (record not deleted). The component should no longer appear in the active list.

title: Create payroll run — DRAFT status; duplicate active run for same period rejected 409
preconditions: No existing active run for the period. User has HR.PAYROLL.RUN.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/payroll-runs and click New Run.
2. Enter periodMonth 6, periodYear 2026, payDate 2026-06-30.
3. Save.
4. Attempt to create a second run for the same period (periodMonth 6, periodYear 2026).
expected: 201 Created. PayrollRunDto status = DRAFT, server-generated runNumber, totals zero. Second creation attempt returns 409 ConflictException 'Active payroll run already exists for period ...'.

title: Calculate payroll run — DRAFT to CALCULATED; lines generated per active employee with active contract
preconditions: DRAFT run exists. At least 1 ACTIVE employee with active PERMANENT contract. Statutory sets and PAYE bands seeded (HrStatutorySeeder). User has HR.PAYROLL.RUN.
steps:
1. Open the payroll run detail at /admin/hr/payroll-runs/uid/:uid.
2. Click Calculate.
3. Open the Lines tab.
4. Verify each active employee with an active contract has a line.
5. Verify lines include basic salary earnings and statutory deductions (PAYE, NSSF, HESLB per contract flags).
6. Verify run totals (gross, deduction, net, employer cost) are populated.
testData: Run from HR-022, employees with PERMANENT contracts
expected: Status = CALCULATED. One line per eligible employee. Lines show earning and deduction items. Employees without an active contract are skipped. Run-level totals match the sum of lines.

title: Calculate from POSTED/PAID/REVERSED is rejected 409; recalculate from CALCULATED or APPROVED is allowed
preconditions: Runs in POSTED, PAID, REVERSED, CALCULATED, and APPROVED statuses. User has HR.PAYROLL.RUN.
steps:
1. Attempt calculate on a POSTED run — expect 409.
2. Attempt calculate on a PAID run — expect 409.
3. Attempt calculate on a REVERSED run — expect 409.
4. Calculate on a CALCULATED run — expect success (idempotent rebuild, prior lines deleted).
5. Calculate on an APPROVED run — expect success.
expected: POSTED/PAID/REVERSED returns 409. CALCULATED and APPROVED both succeed (idempotent), resetting status to CALCULATED and rebuilding lines.

title: Negative-net payroll line is FLAGGED and blocks approval
preconditions: An employee whose total deductions exceed gross (e.g. large loan installment). CALCULATED run. User has HR.PAYROLL.RUN and HR.PAYROLL.APPROVE.
steps:
1. Calculate the run.
2. Find the flagged employee line — verify PayrollLineStatus = FLAGGED and a reason containing 'Net amount negative after deductions'.
3. Attempt to approve the run.
4. Verify 409 listing the flagged employees.
5. Reduce the loan installment, recalculate, and verify the line is now OK.
6. Approve successfully.
expected: Line status = FLAGGED. Approve returns 409 'Cannot approve run with FLAGGED payroll lines. Resolve: ...' listing the employee. After fixing, line = OK and approve succeeds (status = APPROVED).

title: Approve payroll run — CALCULATED to APPROVED; RUN-only user denied
preconditions: A CALCULATED run with no flagged lines. Two users: HR.PAYROLL.APPROVE and HR.PAYROLL.RUN only.
steps:
1. Log in as HR.PAYROLL.APPROVE user.
2. Open the run detail and click Approve.
3. Verify status = APPROVED and approvedAt/approvedBy are stamped.
4. Attempt approve with the RUN-only user — verify 403.
expected: Status = APPROVED. approvedAt and approvedBy populated. RUN-only user gets 403. Approve from DRAFT returns 409.

title: Post payroll run — APPROVED to POSTED; GL posting event published; payslips generated
preconditions: An APPROVED payroll run. GL config keys resolvable. User has HR.PAYROLL.POST.
steps:
1. Open the APPROVED run detail.
2. Click Post.
3. Verify status = POSTED and postedAt/postedBy stamped.
4. Verify the PAYROLL_FINALISED outbox event was published (visible in domain_event table).
5. Verify payslips were generated — one per payroll line (payslipNumber PAYSLIP-#####).
expected: Status = POSTED. postedAt populated. PAYROLL_FINALISED outbox event row visible. Payslips created one per line with auto-generated numbers. Post from CALCULATED returns 409.

title: Disburse payroll run — POSTED to PAID; Cash and Bank OUT entry created
preconditions: A POSTED run with netTotal > 0. A Cash and Bank account exists. User has HR.PAYROLL.DISBURSE.
steps:
1. Open the POSTED run detail.
2. Click Disburse.
3. Select the cash/bank account by name (uid-picker).
4. Leave txnDate blank (defaults to payDate).
5. Submit.
6. Verify status = PAID and paidAt stamped.
7. Verify a Cash and Bank OUT direct entry was recorded (DR NET_WAGES_PAYABLE / CR bank GL).
testData: POSTED run from HR-027; Cash and Bank account by name
expected: Status = PAID. paidAt populated. Cash and Bank OUT entry visible with memo 'Net wages disbursement for <runNumber>'. Disburse from non-POSTED status returns 409. netTotal <= 0 returns 409. Blank cashBankAccountUid returns 400.

title: Reverse payroll run — POSTED to REVERSED and PAID to REVERSED; PAYROLL_REVERSED event published
preconditions: One POSTED run and one PAID run. User has HR.PAYROLL.REVERSE.
steps:
1. Open the POSTED run and click Reverse — verify status = REVERSED and reversedAt stamped.
2. Open the PAID run and click Reverse — verify status = REVERSED.
3. Verify PAYROLL_REVERSED outbox event published for each reversal.
4. Attempt to reverse an already-REVERSED run — expect 409.
5. Attempt reverse on DRAFT/CALCULATED/APPROVED — expect 409.
testData: One POSTED run (HR-027), one PAID run (HR-028)
expected: Both POSTED and PAID runs transition to REVERSED. reversedAt stamped. PAYROLL_REVERSED outbox event created. Already-REVERSED returns 409. DRAFT/CALCULATED/APPROVED returns 409 'Only POSTED or PAID payroll runs can be reversed'.

title: Payroll RBAC split — each action permission grants only its own action, all others denied
preconditions: Six users each holding exactly one of: HR.PAYROLL.VIEW, HR.PAYROLL.RUN, HR.PAYROLL.APPROVE, HR.PAYROLL.POST, HR.PAYROLL.DISBURSE, HR.PAYROLL.REVERSE. Runs prepared in matching statuses.
steps:
1. For each single-permission user, open the run in the matching status and verify only the expected action button is visible.
2. Attempt all other actions via direct API calls and verify 403 for each.
3. Verify VIEW-only user sees the run and lines but no action buttons.
expected: Each unauthorized action returns 403. UI hides buttons that the user lacks permission for. VIEW-only user: read-only, no action buttons rendered.

title: Create PAYE band set — multiple bands with ascending bandNo
preconditions: User has HR.STATUTORY.MANAGE. A company is selected.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/hr/statutory.
2. Click New PAYE Band Set.
3. Enter effectiveFrom 2026-01-01, taxFreeThreshold 270000.
4. Add band 1: lowerBound 270000, marginalRate 0.08, cumulativeFixedTax 0.
5. Add band 2: lowerBound 520000, marginalRate 0.20, cumulativeFixedTax 20000.
6. Save.
expected: 201 Created. PayeBandSetDto returned with the two bands, each assigned uids. Appears in the PAYE band sets list. Missing effectiveFrom or taxFreeThreshold returns 400.

title: Create statutory rate sets for NSSF, WCF, SDL, and HESLB
preconditions: User has HR.STATUTORY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Create NSSF rate set: rateType NSSF, effectiveFrom 2026-01-01, employeeRate 0.10, employerRate 0.10, basis GROSS.
2. Create WCF: rateType WCF, employerRate 0.005, basis GROSS.
3. Create SDL: rateType SDL, employerRate 0.035, headcountThreshold 10, basis GROSS.
4. Create HESLB: rateType HESLB, employeeRate 0.15, basis BASIC.
5. Verify each appears in the rate sets list with the correct type and rates.
testData: NSSF, WCF, SDL, HESLB rate sets as described
expected: Four 201 Created responses. Each StatutoryRateSetDto carries the correct rateType, rates, basis, and active = true. SDL retains headcountThreshold 10. Missing rateType or effectiveFrom returns 400.

title: Statutory rate sets drive payroll calculation — contract flags gate which apply
preconditions: Active PAYE band set and NSSF/WCF/SDL/HESLB rate sets effective on the run payDate. Employee A has nssfMember=true, payeResident=true. Employee B has nssfMember=false, payeResident=false.
steps:
1. Calculate the payroll run.
2. For employee A: verify PAYE, NSSF, and applicable levies appear as deduction/employer-cost lines.
3. For employee B: verify NSSF line is zero/absent and PAYE is zero/absent based on flags.
4. Verify the statutory snapshot uid is captured on each line (reproducibility).
testData: Two employees with different statutory flag combinations
expected: Employee A has PAYE computed per the PAYE band, NSSF at 10% employee + 10% employer. Employee B's NSSF and PAYE are zero because nssfMember=false/payeResident=false. Statutory snapshot uid present on each line.

title: Statutory RBAC — user without HR.STATUTORY.MANAGE is denied
preconditions: A user with only HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW (no HR.STATUTORY.MANAGE).
steps:
1. Log in as the restricted user.
2. Confirm the Statutory Setup nav item is hidden.
3. Attempt to navigate directly to /admin/hr/statutory.
4. Attempt POST /api/v1/hr/statutory/paye-bands with the user's token.
expected: Nav item hidden. Route guard blocks navigation. POST to the API returns 403.

title: HR nav visibility — correct items shown per permission subset
preconditions: Three users: (a) no permissions, (b) HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW only, (c) full HR permission set.
steps:
1. Log in as user (a) — verify the HR & Payroll nav group is entirely hidden.
2. Log in as user (b) with HR.EMPLOYEE.VIEW — verify only Employees, Departments, and Employee Contracts are visible; Pay Components, Payroll Runs, Leave, Loans, Statutory Setup are hidden.
3. Log in as user (c) with all HR permissions — verify all eight nav items are visible.
testData: Three users with the described permission sets
expected: (a) No HR group visible. (b) Only VIEW-gated items visible (Employees, Departments, Contracts). (c) All eight items visible. Direct route to a hidden item triggers the route guard forbidden state.

title: Branch scoping — acting in an unassigned branch is denied for all HR endpoints
preconditions: Multi-branch company. User assigned to branch B1 only (HR permissions granted).
steps:
1. Set active branch to B1 (X-Branch-Uid header) and list employees — succeeds.
2. Switch active branch to B2 (not assigned) and attempt GET /api/v1/hr/employees.
3. Verify 403 returned by ScopeGuard.assertCanActIn.
expected: Acting in B1 succeeds. Acting in B2 returns 403. A user assigned to ALL branches succeeds in any branch.

title: Money and date formatting across all HR screens
preconditions: HR data seeded: contract with baseSalary, loan amounts, payroll totals, leave dates, pay dates.
steps:
1. Navigate through contracts, loans, payroll runs, leave requests, and statutory screens.
2. Inspect contract base salary display.
3. Inspect loan principal, installment, and outstanding amount display.
4. Inspect payroll run totals and net amounts on the lines tab.
5. Inspect all date fields (hireDate, startDate, fromDate, toDate, payDate).
expected: All money rendered as 'TZS 1,500,000.00' format (currency string prefix, two decimal places). Dates rendered in ISO yyyy-MM-dd format. Flagged lines with negative net still format the amount correctly.

title: Lead list — pagination, company scope, four states, no raw uid in cells
preconditions: At least 21 leads in the company to force 2 pages. User has CRM.LEAD.VIEW.
steps:
1. Log in as ORG_ADMIN and navigate to /admin/crm/leads.
2. Confirm the company auto-selects and the list loads.
3. Observe the loading state transitioning to idle with rows showing leadNumber, displayName, status badge, source.
4. Use paginator controls: NEXT, page 2, PREVIOUS, FIRST, LAST.
5. Log in as NO-PERMISSION user, confirm CRM > Leads nav item is absent, and direct route is blocked.
expected: Table shows lead rows. Meta: page=1, size=20, totalElements=21, totalPages=2, hasNext=true. Paginator visible. No raw uid in any cell. NO-PERMISSION user: nav hidden, route forbidden, API 403.

title: Create lead — all LeadSource values; MANAGE permission required
preconditions: At least one company exists. User has CRM.LEAD.MANAGE. A VIEW-only user also available.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/leads and click New Lead.
2. Fill displayName 'Acme Trading', leadSource REFERRAL, phone '+255700000001', email 'buyer@acme.test'.
3. Submit and verify 201 with leadNumber LEAD-0001 and status NEW.
4. Repeat for each remaining LeadSource: WEBSITE, WALK_IN, CAMPAIGN, COLD_CALL, EXISTING_CUSTOMER, OTHER.
5. Log in as VIEW-only user and verify New Lead button is hidden; direct POST returns 403.
testData: displayName: Acme Trading, leadSource: REFERRAL (and all other LeadSource values)
expected: 201 for each. leadNumber generated in LEAD-#### format. status = NEW. branchId stamped from active-branch context. VIEW-only user: button hidden, 403 on direct POST.

title: Lead lifecycle — NEW to CONTACTED; contact action rejected on non-NEW leads
preconditions: A NEW lead. User has CRM.LEAD.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the lead at /admin/crm/leads/uid/:uid.
2. Click 'Mark as contacted'.
3. Verify status = CONTACTED and the button is now hidden/disabled.
4. Attempt to contact the already-CONTACTED lead via direct API call.
expected: Status = CONTACTED. canContact = false after transition so button hidden. Direct API on CONTACTED lead returns error 'Only NEW leads can move to CONTACTED'.

title: Qualify lead by linking existing customer — status QUALIFIED; QUALIFY permission required
preconditions: A NEW or CONTACTED lead. An existing Parties customer in the same company. User has CRM.LEAD.QUALIFY. A second user has MANAGE but not QUALIFY.
steps:
1. Open the lead detail.
2. Open the Qualify form and choose 'Link existing customer'.
3. Select the customer 'Zanaco Ltd' by name from the picker (not by uid).
4. Submit.
5. Verify status = QUALIFIED, customerUid set, qualifiedAt stamped.
6. Log in as MANAGE-only user and attempt qualify — verify 403.
expected: Status = QUALIFIED. customerUid and qualifiedAt populated. Badge text-bg-primary. MANAGE-only user gets 403. Customer from another tenant returns ScopeGuard 403.

title: Qualify lead by promoting new customer — CREDIT_ACCOUNT and CASH_WALK_IN kinds
preconditions: A NEW or CONTACTED lead. User has CRM.LEAD.QUALIFY.
steps:
1. Open the Qualify form; choose 'Create new customer'.
2. Enter customer name 'Mlimani Hardware', customerKind CREDIT_ACCOUNT, phone '+255700000099'.
3. Submit and verify a new Parties customer was created and the lead is QUALIFIED.
4. Repeat with customerKind CASH_WALK_IN on a different lead.
testData: name: Mlimani Hardware, kind: CREDIT_ACCOUNT; second pass with CASH_WALK_IN
expected: A new Parties customer created by CustomerService. Lead status = QUALIFIED linked to the new customer. qualifiedAt stamped. Blank customer name returns 400 on client validation.

title: Disqualify lead — reason required; terminal leads cannot be re-disqualified
preconditions: A non-terminal lead (NEW, CONTACTED, or QUALIFIED). User has CRM.LEAD.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the lead detail.
2. Open Disqualify form, enter reason 'Budget too low', submit.
3. Verify status = DISQUALIFIED, disqualifyReason and disqualifiedAt set.
4. Attempt to disqualify an already-DISQUALIFIED lead — expect error.
5. Attempt with a blank reason — expect client validation.
expected: Status = DISQUALIFIED. disqualifyReason and disqualifiedAt populated. Blank reason: client 'Reason is required.' + server 400 @NotBlank. Disqualifying a terminal lead returns 'Cannot disqualify a terminal lead'.

title: Edit blocked on CONVERTED and DISQUALIFIED terminal leads
preconditions: One NEW lead and one DISQUALIFIED lead. User has CRM.LEAD.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Edit fields on the NEW lead and save — verify success.
2. Open the DISQUALIFIED lead — verify edit controls are disabled (canEdit = !isTerminal && canManage).
3. Force a direct PUT to the DISQUALIFIED lead's endpoint.
testData: New lead editable; DISQUALIFIED lead should be locked
expected: NEW lead edit persists. DISQUALIFIED lead: controls disabled, forced PUT returns 'Cannot edit a terminal lead'.

title: Qualified lead transitions to CONVERTED when an opportunity is created from it
preconditions: A QUALIFIED lead. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/opportunities/create.
2. The source-lead picker lists only QUALIFIED leads — select the lead by name.
3. Complete the opportunity form and submit.
4. Verify the source lead's status is now CONVERTED with convertedAt set.
testData: A QUALIFIED lead, valid opportunity details
expected: Opportunity created successfully. Source lead status = CONVERTED, convertedAt stamped. Attempting to attach a non-QUALIFIED (e.g. NEW) lead returns 'Source lead must be QUALIFIED to create an opportunity'.

title: Opportunity list — pagination, company scope, four states
preconditions: At least 21 opportunities. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.VIEW.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/opportunities.
2. Observe loading to idle transition.
3. Verify rows show opportunityNumber, title, customer name, status badge, estimated value formatted as currency.
4. Navigate paginator controls.
5. Test NO-PERMISSION user: nav hidden, route forbidden, API 403.
expected: Meta totalPages >= 2. Money formatted 'TZS 1,234.56'. Paginator visible. NO-PERMISSION: 403 on API.

title: Create opportunity — customer and stage via name pickers; probability inherits from stage
preconditions: A customer and active pipeline stages (seeded by V51) in the company. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/opportunities/create.
2. Pick customer 'Zanaco Ltd' by name.
3. Select pipeline stage 'PROPOSAL' (defaultProbability 50).
4. Enter title 'Q3 hardware refresh', currency TZS, estimatedValue 5000000.
5. Submit.
6. Verify redirect to /admin/crm/opportunities/uid/:uid.
7. Verify status OPEN, winProbability 50 (inherited from stage).
testData: title: Q3 hardware refresh, customer: Zanaco Ltd, stage: PROPOSAL, estimatedValue: 5000000
expected: 201 Created. Redirect to detail. status = OPEN. winProbability = 50. opportunityNumber generated. Deactivated stage returns 'Pipeline stage is deactivated'. Stage from another company returns rejection.

title: Add opportunity line — product search and unit picker; qty and discount validation
preconditions: An OPEN opportunity. At least 1 product and ACTIVE unit-of-measure in the company. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the opportunity detail.
2. In the Add-line form, search for product 'WIDGET-01 — Widget' (debounced 300ms) and select it.
3. Select unit 'EACH' from the active units dropdown.
4. Enter qty 10, unitPrice 2500, discount% 5.
5. Add the line.
6. Attempt to add a line with qty 0 — verify rejection.
7. Attempt discount% of 110 — verify rejection.
testData: product: WIDGET-01, unit: EACH, qty: 10, unitPrice: 2500, discount: 5
expected: Line appended with auto-incremented line_no. Product and unit shown by name not uid. qty = 0 returns 400 (@DecimalMin). discount% 110 returns 400 (chk_opportunity_line_disc). Add-line on WON/LOST opportunity returns 'Cannot modify a closed opportunity'.

title: Advance opportunity stage — probability follows stage default or is overridden
preconditions: An OPEN opportunity at PROPOSAL stage. At least 2 active pipeline stages. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the Advance-stage form.
2. Select stage 'NEGOTIATION' (default probability 75) — submit.
3. Verify pipelineStageId updated and winProbability = 75.
4. Advance again with a manual probability override of 80.
5. Verify winProbability = 80.
testData: Target stage: NEGOTIATION (prob 75); second pass with probability override 80
expected: Stage updated. Default probability applied when no override. Override applied when supplied. Advance on WON/LOST returns 'Cannot modify a closed opportunity'. Deactivated target stage is rejected.

title: Win opportunity — OPEN to WON; wonAt stamped; only OPEN can be won
preconditions: An OPEN opportunity. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the Win form.
2. Set won-at date (optional — defaults to now if blank).
3. Submit.
4. Verify status = WON and wonAt stamped.
5. Attempt to win an already-WON opportunity — expect rejection.
expected: Status = WON. wonAt populated. Edit/add-line/advance/win/lose actions hidden. Convert still available. Winning a non-OPEN opportunity returns 'Only OPEN opportunities can be won'.

title: Lose opportunity — loss reason required; only OPEN can be lost
preconditions: An OPEN opportunity. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the Lose form.
2. Enter lossReason 'Lost to competitor on price'.
3. Submit.
4. Verify status = LOST and lostAt + lossReason set.
5. Attempt to lose an already-LOST opportunity.
6. Attempt with a blank reason.
testData: lossReason: Lost to competitor on price
expected: Status = LOST. lostAt and lossReason populated. Blank reason: client validation + server 400 @NotBlank. Non-OPEN opportunity returns 'Only OPEN opportunities can be lost'.

title: Convert OPEN opportunity to QUOTATION — CONVERT permission required; zero lines blocked
preconditions: An OPEN opportunity with at least one line. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.CONVERT. A second user has MANAGE but not CONVERT.
steps:
1. Open the Convert form; choose target QUOTATION.
2. Submit.
3. Verify a Quotation is created with lines copied; convertedDocumentKind = QUOTATION + document number shown.
4. Verify 'Open document' link navigates to /admin/quotations/uid/:uid.
5. Log in as MANAGE-without-CONVERT user and attempt convert — expect 403.
6. Attempt convert on an opportunity with 0 lines — expect rejection.
expected: Quotation created. convertedDocumentKind = QUOTATION. Link navigates to the quotation. MANAGE-without-CONVERT user gets 403. Zero lines: 'Opportunity has no lines'. LOST opportunity convert to QUOTATION rejected.

title: Convert WON opportunity to SALES_ORDER — requires WON status
preconditions: A WON opportunity with at least one line. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.CONVERT.
steps:
1. On the WON opportunity, open Convert form; choose SALES_ORDER.
2. Convert.
3. Verify Sales Order created with lines copied; link navigates to /admin/sales-orders/uid/:uid.
4. Attempt SALES_ORDER convert while opportunity is OPEN (not WON).
expected: Sales Order created. convertedDocumentKind = SALES_ORDER. Link points to the SO. Convert to SALES_ORDER on OPEN returns 'Converting to a SALES_ORDER requires the opportunity to be WON'.

title: Convert is idempotent — second convert returns the first document, no duplicate
preconditions: An already-converted opportunity. User has CRM.OPPORTUNITY.CONVERT.
steps:
1. Invoke convert again on the same already-converted opportunity.
2. Verify no second document is created.
3. Verify the response returns the original convertedDocumentKind and convertedDocumentUid.
expected: No duplicate document. Returns the original convertedDocumentKind and convertedDocumentUid. Document number is null on the repeat response (idempotent return). DB unique constraint uq_opportunity_converted_document backstops any race.

title: Pipeline board — summary by stage; company + branch scoped
preconditions: Open opportunities across multiple pipeline stages in the default branch. User has CRM.PIPELINE.VIEW.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/pipeline.
2. Confirm first company and first branch auto-select.
3. Observe the stage board with counts and estimated values per stage.
4. Switch active branch and verify the board re-scopes.
5. Log in as NO-PERMISSION user — verify nav hidden and API 403.
testData: Opportunities in at least 3 different stages
expected: PipelineSummaryDto rendered grouped by stage with count and total value. Correct company+branch scope. NO-PERMISSION: 403. User not assigned to selected branch gets scope enforcement error.

title: Pipeline forecast — weighted by probability over date range
preconditions: Open opportunities with expectedCloseDate inside a 3-month window and win probabilities set. User has CRM.PIPELINE.VIEW.
steps:
1. Open the pipeline dashboard.
2. Observe forecast for the default date range (current month to +3 months).
3. Adjust From and To dates and click Apply.
4. Verify ForecastDto weighted forecast updates for the new range.
testData: from: first day of current month, to: 3 months out
expected: Weighted forecast values displayed. Range adjustment triggers a refetch. Dates in ISO yyyy-MM-dd. Missing from or to: no fetch (client guard). Inverted range (from > to): empty or edge result.

title: Pipeline KPIs — win-rate and cycle-time; zero-deal period shows zeros not error
preconditions: Some WON and LOST opportunities in the period. User has CRM.PIPELINE.VIEW.
steps:
1. Open the pipeline dashboard KPI panel.
2. Verify win-rate (%) and average cycle-time are displayed.
3. Adjust dates to a period with no closed deals — verify zeros displayed, not an error state.
testData: Period with WON + LOST deals; then a period with no closed deals
expected: CrmKpiDto: win-rate and avg cycle-time shown for the period with data. Zero-deal period returns zeros, not an error. Loading/idle states distinct.

title: Pipeline stages list — V51-seeded stages shown in displayOrder; not paginated
preconditions: V51 migration seeded 5 stages per company: QUALIFICATION (order 1), NEEDS_ANALYSIS (2), PROPOSAL (3), NEGOTIATION (4), CLOSING (5). User has CRM.STAGE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/settings/pipeline-stages.
2. Observe the list ordered by displayOrder.
3. Verify no paginator is present (intentionally unpaginated — bare array response).
testData: Company seeded with 5 stages from V51
expected: Five stages listed in displayOrder 1-5. No paginator rendered. Loading/empty/error/forbidden states handled. Route guard requires CRM.STAGE.MANAGE (not just OPPORTUNITY.VIEW).

title: Create pipeline stage — unique name and displayOrder enforced; probability 0-100
preconditions: A company with the 5 seeded stages. User has CRM.STAGE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Click New Stage.
2. Enter name DEMO, displayOrder 6, defaultProbability 40.
3. Submit.
4. Attempt to create a duplicate name 'PROPOSAL'.
5. Attempt defaultProbability of 110.
expected: 201 Created. Stage DEMO appears in list. Duplicate name returns 'Pipeline stage name already exists'. Probability 110 returns client + server 400 (chk_pipeline_stage_probability). Duplicate displayOrder returns DB constraint error.

title: Deactivate pipeline stage — soft-delete; deactivated stage rejected on new opportunity/advance
preconditions: A stage exists. An open opportunity create flow available. User has CRM.STAGE.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Deactivate the DEMO stage (DELETE endpoint).
2. Verify 204 and isActive = false (record not removed).
3. Confirm DEMO disappears from the active-stage dropdowns in opportunity create/advance.
4. Attempt to create an opportunity with the deactivated stage uid via direct API.
expected: 204 No Content. Stage ACTIVE flag = false. Stage absent from active-stage pickers (UI filters s.active). Direct API with deactivated stage uid returns 'Pipeline stage is deactivated'.

title: Log CALL, EMAIL, MEETING, NOTE on a lead — subject required, no due date/assignee for non-TASK
preconditions: A lead exists. User has CRM.ACTIVITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open lead detail; in the activity panel click Log Activity.
2. Choose type CALL; enter subject 'Intro call', body 'Discussed needs'; submit.
3. Verify the activity appears at top of the by-lead list (latest-first).
4. Repeat for EMAIL, MEETING, NOTE types.
5. Attempt to send dueDate on a CALL type — expect rejection.
testData: type: CALL, subject: Intro call, body: Discussed needs
expected: 201 for each non-TASK type. Activity appears in by-lead list. No dueDate or assignee on non-TASK. Sending dueDate on non-TASK returns 'Only TASK activities may have due_date or assigneeUserId'. Blank subject returns 400.

title: Log TASK on an opportunity — dueDate required; surfaces in open-task inbox
preconditions: An opportunity exists. User has CRM.ACTIVITY.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open opportunity detail; in the activity panel choose type TASK (dueDate field appears via isTask).
2. Enter subject 'Send proposal', dueDate 2026-07-01.
3. Submit.
4. Navigate to /admin/crm/activities open-task inbox and verify the task appears.
testData: type: TASK, subject: Send proposal, dueDate: 2026-07-01
expected: 201 Created. TASK appears in by-opportunity list. Task surfaces in the open-task inbox. TASK without dueDate returns 'TASK activities must have a due_date.' Providing both leadUid and opportunityUid returns 'Exactly one of leadUid or opportunityUid must be provided.'

title: Complete a TASK from the open-task inbox; non-TASK and already-done rejected
preconditions: At least 21 open TASK activities (2+ pages). User has CRM.ACTIVITY.VIEW (list) and CRM.ACTIVITY.MANAGE (complete).
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/crm/activities.
2. Observe the paginated open-tasks list (only done=false TASKs).
3. Navigate paginator controls.
4. Click Complete on a task row.
5. Verify the task disappears from the inbox and success toast shown.
6. Attempt to complete a non-TASK activity — expect rejection.
7. Attempt to complete the already-completed task — expect rejection.
expected: Only open TASKs listed. Paginator visible. On complete: task removed from inbox, list reloads. Complete on non-TASK: 'Only TASK activities can be completed'. Complete on already-done: 'Activity is already done.' VIEW-only user: Complete button hidden, API 403.

title: Activity panel — paginated by-lead and by-opportunity lists; cross-tenant lead denied
preconditions: At least 11 activities on one lead (panel size 10). User has CRM.ACTIVITY.VIEW.
steps:
1. Open the lead detail with 11+ activities.
2. Verify the activity panel paginates (size 10), ordered occurredAt descending.
3. Attempt to access activities panel for a lead belonging to another tenant.
expected: Activities paged at size 10, ordered latest-first. Paginator visible. Meta reflects totals. Cross-tenant lead uid returns 403 (scoped on lead uid). Empty lead: empty panel state.

title: Multi-tenant isolation — tenant A cannot access tenant B CRM records
preconditions: Two organisations each with leads, opportunities, stages, and activities. Tenant A user has full CRM permissions.
steps:
1. As tenant-A user, list leads for company A — confirm only A's records appear.
2. Attempt GET /api/v1/crm/leads/uid/{B-lead} — expect 403.
3. Attempt list leads with companyId of tenant B — expect 403.
4. Attempt GET on a tenant-B opportunity uid — expect 403.
5. Attempt list activities for a tenant-B lead uid — expect 403.
testData: Tenant A and Tenant B CRM record uids
expected: Every cross-tenant access returns 403 (ScopeGuard). No tenant-B data ever appears for tenant-A user. rootadmin can cross tenants (positive control to validate the guard is specific to non-superusers).

title: RBAC matrix — each CRM action denied for role missing exactly that permission
preconditions: Custom roles: one per assertion, each granted all CRM permissions except the one under test.
steps:
1. CRM.LEAD.MANAGE absent: create/contact/disqualify lead — all 403; nav item hidden.
2. CRM.LEAD.QUALIFY absent: qualify action hidden, API 403.
3. CRM.OPPORTUNITY.MANAGE absent: create/edit/win/lose/advance — all 403.
4. CRM.OPPORTUNITY.CONVERT absent: convert hidden, API 403.
5. CRM.ACTIVITY.MANAGE absent: log/complete actions hidden, API 403.
6. CRM.STAGE.MANAGE absent: stage settings route forbidden, create/edit/deactivate 403.
7. CRM.PIPELINE.VIEW absent: pipeline nav hidden, API 403.
expected: Each action returns 403 when the required permission is absent. UI control hidden per canX computed signals. Cross-gate: stage list/getByUid use CRM.OPPORTUNITY.VIEW — a STAGE.MANAGE-only role without OPPORTUNITY.VIEW cannot hit them.

title: uid never shown to users — all CRM resources chosen by name via picker
preconditions: Full CRM permissions as ORG_ADMIN. Several leads, opportunities, stages, and activities seeded.
steps:
1. Scan all CRM screens (leads list/detail, opportunity create/detail, stages list, activities panel and inbox) for any raw 26-character uid in visible text.
2. Verify every cross-resource reference (customer, source lead, product, pipeline stage) is presented as a human name or code in the picker.
3. Verify uid appears only in /admin/.../uid/:uid URL paths.
expected: No raw uid visible in tables, labels, or detail text. All pickers show name/code labels. Resource numbers (LEAD-0001, OPP-0001) are shown in place of uids. Pickers are keyboard-operable and labelled for accessibility.

title: Projects nav group visible only with correct permissions; WIP Report gated separately
preconditions: Three users: ORG_ADMIN (all PROJECTS.*), COSTING-only user (PROJECTS.COSTING.VIEW only), NO-PERMISSION user.
steps:
1. Log in as ORG_ADMIN — expand Projects nav group, verify both 'Projects' and 'WIP Report' links are present.
2. Log in as COSTING-only user — verify 'WIP Report' visible but 'Projects' link absent.
3. Log in as NO-PERMISSION user — verify the entire Projects nav group is absent.
testData: Three users with the described permission sets
expected: ORG_ADMIN sees both links. COSTING-only sees WIP Report but not Projects list. NO-PERMISSION sees neither. Axe scan clean on nav for ORG_ADMIN.

title: Project list — four states, pagination, company scope; CREATE button gated
preconditions: At least 21 ACTIVE projects in the company (to force 2 pages). User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.VIEW. A second user has VIEW only (no CREATE).
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/projects as ORG_ADMIN.
2. Observe loading to idle; table shows Project #, name, status badge, dates, budget.
3. Use paginator: FIRST, PREVIOUS, page numbers, NEXT, LAST.
4. Confirm company selector scopes the list.
5. Log in as VIEW-only user — verify New Project button is absent; direct POST returns 403.
expected: Meta: totalPages >= 2, hasNext = true on page 1. Money formatted 'TZS n,nnn.nn'. Paginator visible. VIEW-only user: New Project hidden, POST 403.

title: Create project — minimal name only; project number PRJ-#### generated
preconditions: A company with a default branch exists. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.CREATE.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/projects.
2. Click New Project (visible when canCreate).
3. Enter name 'Office Fit-out 2026'; leave dates, budget, notes blank.
4. Submit.
5. Verify success alert shows the project number.
6. Verify the list reloads with the new project.
expected: 200/201 with ProjectDto. projectNumber format PRJ-####. projectStatus = DRAFT. status (MasterStatus) = ACTIVE. currency defaults to company base currency (TZS). Success alert shows project number, not uid. Blank name returns client 'Project name is required.' Name > 160 chars returns server 400.

title: Edit project — set customer and manager via name pickers; cross-company customer rejected
preconditions: A DRAFT project. A BUSINESS/CREDIT_ACCOUNT customer and a user to be manager both in the same company. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open project detail at /admin/projects/uid/:uid.
2. In the edit panel, open Customer uid-picker and select 'Acme Traders Ltd' by display name.
3. Open Manager uid-picker and select 'Jane Mwita' by name.
4. Change name, planned dates, budget, notes.
5. Save.
6. Attempt with a customer uid from a different company.
testData: customer: Acme Traders Ltd, manager: Jane Mwita, name: Office Fit-out 2026 (rev B), start: 2026-07-01, end: 2026-12-31, budget: 15000000
expected: PUT succeeds. customerId and managerUserId populated. No raw uid shown — selection was by name. Cross-company customer returns NotFoundException 404. Blank name returns client validation. Name > 160 chars returns 400.

title: Archive project — MasterStatus becomes ARCHIVED; hidden from default list filter
preconditions: An existing project. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Open the project detail and click Archive.
2. Verify success alert; header status badge shows ARCHIVED.
3. Navigate to /admin/projects — confirm project absent from default (ACTIVE MasterStatus) list.
4. Confirm project retrieved via status=ARCHIVED query param.
expected: PATCH .../archive sets status = ARCHIVED. Audit PROJECT_ARCHIVE recorded. Project hidden from default list. Retrievable via status=ARCHIVED filter. Archiving an already-archived project is idempotent.

title: Project lifecycle — full legal path: DRAFT -> ACTIVE -> ON_HOLD -> ACTIVE -> COMPLETED
preconditions: A DRAFT project. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. DRAFT project: click Activate → verify projectStatus = ACTIVE, activatedAt stamped.
2. ACTIVE project: click Hold → verify status = ON_HOLD.
3. ON_HOLD project: click Resume → verify status = ACTIVE again.
4. ACTIVE project: click Complete → verify status = COMPLETED, completedAt stamped, lifecycle buttons hidden (isTerminal).
testData: Single project progressed through each state
expected: Each transition succeeds. Timestamps stamped per transition. Audit PROJECT_STATUS_CHANGE events created. On COMPLETED: no further lifecycle buttons rendered. ON_HOLD → COMPLETED also valid (separate positive control).

title: Cancel project from DRAFT, ACTIVE, and ON_HOLD; CANCELLED is terminal
preconditions: Three projects: one each in DRAFT, ACTIVE, ON_HOLD. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. Cancel the DRAFT project — verify CANCELLED and cancelledAt stamped.
2. Cancel the ACTIVE project — verify CANCELLED.
3. Cancel the ON_HOLD project — verify CANCELLED.
4. Attempt any transition from a CANCELLED project — expect rejection.
expected: All three move to CANCELLED. cancelledAt stamped for each. Audited. CANCELLED → any transition returns IllegalStateException. UI offers no lifecycle buttons when CANCELLED (isTerminal).

title: Illegal project transitions — exhaustive matrix rejected with error
preconditions: Projects in each of the five statuses. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. DRAFT → ON_HOLD — reject.
2. DRAFT → COMPLETED — reject.
3. ACTIVE → DRAFT — reject.
4. ACTIVE → ACTIVE (self-transition) — reject.
5. ON_HOLD → ON_HOLD — reject.
6. COMPLETED → ACTIVE, ON_HOLD, COMPLETED, CANCELLED — all reject.
7. CANCELLED → any status — all reject.
8. Any state → DRAFT — reject.
expected: Every listed call returns error (IllegalStateException surfaced in ApiResponse.errors). Project status unchanged in each case. The UI never offers these illegal buttons.

title: Lifecycle buttons rendered per current status — correct set, aria-labels present
preconditions: Projects in each of DRAFT, ACTIVE, ON_HOLD, COMPLETED, CANCELLED. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE.
steps:
1. DRAFT detail: verify only Activate and Cancel buttons are offered.
2. ACTIVE detail: verify Hold, Complete, Cancel are offered.
3. ON_HOLD detail: verify Resume, Complete, Cancel are offered.
4. COMPLETED and CANCELLED details: verify no lifecycle buttons are rendered.
5. For each button present, verify it has an aria-label ('Activate project', 'Hold project', etc.).
expected: Exact button set per status. No Hold/Complete/Resume on DRAFT. Terminal states have no buttons. Each button has a descriptive aria-label. VIEW-only user sees no lifecycle buttons.

title: Create project task — code, name, planned hours, billable flag
preconditions: An ACTIVE project. User has PROJECTS.TASK.MANAGE (scoped on project).
steps:
1. Open the project detail; in the Tasks panel click Add Task.
2. Enter taskCode 'SITE-PREP', name 'Site preparation', plannedHours 40, billable = true.
3. Save.
4. Verify task appears in the panel with status ACTIVE.
testData: taskCode: SITE-PREP, name: Site preparation, plannedHours: 40, billable: true
expected: 201 Created. ProjectTaskDto with status = ACTIVE, parentId = null. Task visible in panel. Audit PROJECT_TASK_CREATE. Blank taskCode or name returns client validation. taskCode > 30 chars returns 400. name > 160 chars returns 400.

title: Task list — default filter ACTIVE; INACTIVE filter shows deactivated tasks; no paginator
preconditions: A project with at least 1 ACTIVE and 1 INACTIVE (deactivated) task. User has PROJECTS.TASK.VIEW.
steps:
1. Open the project detail; Tasks panel shows ACTIVE tasks (default).
2. Verify no paginator on the tasks panel (it is a plain array, not paginated).
3. Via API, GET /api/v1/project-tasks/project/uid/{projectUid}?status=INACTIVE and verify the deactivated task is returned.
testData: Project with ACTIVE and INACTIVE tasks
expected: Default filter returns only ACTIVE tasks. INACTIVE filter returns deactivated tasks. No paginator rendered on the Tasks panel. Response is List<ProjectTaskDto> (no PageMeta).

title: Deactivate project task — soft-delete; INACTIVE excluded from default list
preconditions: A project with an ACTIVE task. User has PROJECTS.TASK.MANAGE.
steps:
1. In the Tasks panel, click Deactivate on the task row.
2. Confirm the task drops out of the ACTIVE default list.
3. Verify the task is still retrievable via status=INACTIVE query.
expected: PATCH .../deactivate sets status = INACTIVE. Audit PROJECT_TASK_DEACTIVATE. Task absent from default list but retrievable via INACTIVE filter. No hard-delete path. Deactivating an already-INACTIVE task is idempotent.

title: Record timesheet at project level — no task; billable flag; hours validation
preconditions: An ACTIVE project. User has PROJECTS.TIMESHEET.RECORD (scoped on project).
steps:
1. Open project detail; in Timesheets panel click Record Time.
2. Enter userId 7, workDate 2026-06-10, hours 6.5, billable = true.
3. Leave projectTaskUid blank (project-level timesheet).
4. Save.
5. Attempt with hours = 0 — expect 400.
6. Attempt with hours negative — expect 400.
expected: 201 Created. ProjectTimesheetDto with projectTaskId = null, status = ACTIVE. hours = 0 returns 400 (@DecimalMin(0.01)). Negative hours returns 400. Missing userId/workDate returns 400. Audit PROJECT_TIMESHEET_RECORD.

title: Record timesheet against a specific task — task chosen by name via picker; cross-project task rejected
preconditions: A project with an ACTIVE task. A second project with a different task. User has PROJECTS.TIMESHEET.RECORD.
steps:
1. In the Record Time form, open the Task uid-picker and choose 'Site preparation' by name (hint = task code).
2. Fill other required fields and save.
3. Verify projectTaskId set to the chosen task's id.
4. Attempt to record a timesheet for project P1 using a task uid from project P2.
testData: Task: Site preparation; cross-project task uid from P2
expected: Timesheet with projectTaskId set. Task chosen by name, uid stored under the hood. Cross-project task returns 404 'Task not found or does not belong to project' (findByUidAndProjectId guard).

title: Timesheets list is paginated — panel paginator visible with 21+ timesheets
preconditions: A project with at least 21 timesheets. User has PROJECTS.TIMESHEET.VIEW (scoped).
steps:
1. Open the project detail; observe the Timesheets panel showing page 1 (size 20).
2. Use the paginator (FIRST, PREVIOUS, page numbers, NEXT, LAST) to navigate.
3. Verify the paginator self-hides when the project has only 1 page of timesheets.
expected: ApiResponse with meta paginated. Paginator drives loadTimesheets(page). Self-hides at 1 page. Empty project: empty-state message. canTimesheetView = false: panel not shown.

title: Issue materials to project — GOODS product with avg cost; COGS GL posted; stock deducted
preconditions: ACTIVE project. At least 1 GOODS product with on-hand stock and established moving-average cost. GL keys (COGS/INVENTORY) configured. User has PROJECTS.ISSUE.CREATE.
steps:
1. Open the ACTIVE project detail; in Issue-to-Job panel click Issue Materials.
2. Add a product line: pick 'Cement 50kg' by name, qty 20, reason 'phase 1 pour'.
3. Submit.
4. Verify success alert shows issueNumber (PJI-#### format).
5. Verify the stock movement ISSUE_TO_PROJECT was created with qty -20.
6. Verify a COGS GL entry (DR COGS / CR INVENTORY) was posted.
testData: product: Cement 50kg, qty: 20, reason: phase 1 pour
expected: IssueToProjectResultDto with issueNumber PJI-####, per-line value at moving average, totalValue, currency, cogsGlEntryUid. Stock movement posts -20 qty tagged with the projectId. GL DR COGS / CR INVENTORY posted. Product shown by name not uid.

title: Issue to non-taggable project rejected — DRAFT, COMPLETED, CANCELLED reject; ON_HOLD allows
preconditions: Projects in DRAFT, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, and ON_HOLD statuses. User has PROJECTS.ISSUE.CREATE.
steps:
1. Attempt to issue materials to a DRAFT project via API (Issue panel hidden by UI isTaggable guard).
2. Attempt for COMPLETED project.
3. Attempt for CANCELLED project.
4. Issue to an ON_HOLD project — verify success.
testData: Product and qty for each attempt
expected: DRAFT/COMPLETED/CANCELLED: IllegalStateException 'Project ... is not open for tagging (status=...)'. No stock movement. No GL post. ON_HOLD: issue succeeds (allowsTagging() = true for ON_HOLD). UI Issue panel is hidden unless isTaggable.

title: Issue with null avg cost — qty still deducted; COGS leg skipped; line value = 0
preconditions: ACTIVE project. A GOODS product with on-hand qty but avg_cost not yet established (no prior receipt valuation). User has PROJECTS.ISSUE.CREATE.
steps:
1. Issue qty 3 of the product with no established avg cost.
2. Verify the stock movement was created with -3 qty.
3. Verify the COGS GL leg was skipped (WARN logged).
4. Verify the line value = 0 and cogsGlEntryUid may be null.
testData: product: New SKU (no avg cost), qty: 3
expected: Per ADR-0020: costIssue returns null → COGS leg skipped (anomaly/WARN logged). Stock movement still posts -3 qty. Line value = 0. No transaction rollback. Mixed batch: costed lines form the COGS leg; zero-cost lines are excluded from it.

title: Issue validation — empty lines, unknown product, cross-tenant project, negative qty
preconditions: ACTIVE project in company A. A company B project uid. User has PROJECTS.ISSUE.CREATE.
steps:
1. POST with empty lines array — expect 400 (@NotEmpty).
2. POST with blank productUid in a line — expect 400 (@NotBlank).
3. POST with null qty in a line — expect 400 (@NotNull).
4. POST with unknown product uid — expect 404 'Product not found'.
5. POST with company-B project uid — expect 404 'Project not found or belongs to a different company'.
6. POST with negative qty — verify deduction magnitude is positive (service takes qty.abs()).
expected: Each case returns the stated error with no stock/GL side effects. Negative qty: the stock deduction still uses the absolute value (positive magnitude).

title: Project P&L report — revenue, cost-by-type, margin, WIP, recon balanced
preconditions: ACTIVE project with at least 1 issue-to-project (MATERIAL cost) and a tagged INCOME posting. Budget set on the project. User has PROJECTS.COSTING.VIEW.
steps:
1. Open the project detail and click 'View P&L' (visible when canCosting).
2. Observe: revenue, totalCost, costByType rows (MATERIAL etc.), margin, marginPct, budget, budgetVariance, wip, and the recon bar.
3. Verify recon.balanced = true.
4. Verify wip = max(0, totalCost - revenue).
5. Attempt to view P&L for a cross-tenant project.
testData: Project with seeded MATERIAL cost and revenue posting
expected: ProjectPnlDto returned. costByType shows MATERIAL row. wip = max(0, cost - revenue). recon.balanced = true (mismatch = bug). Zero-posting project: all zeros, recon still balanced. Cross-tenant project: 403 scoped denied. COSTING.VIEW absent: 'View P&L' button hidden, API 403.

title: WIP report — cross-project totals, four states, no paginator; company scoped
preconditions: At least 2 projects with cost + billing activity in the company. User has PROJECTS.COSTING.VIEW.
steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/projects/wip-report.
2. Select the company and click Load Report.
3. Verify per-project rows (project #, name, cost incurred, billed, WIP).
4. Verify footer totals (sum of cost incurred, billed, WIP).
5. Confirm no paginator is present (response is a plain list, not paginated).
6. Test NO-PERMISSION user: forbidden state distinct from error state.
testData: Company with 2+ active projects having cost and billing
expected: ApiResponse<List<ProjectWipRowDto>>. wip = max(0, costIncurred - billed) per row. Footer totals match. No paginator rendered. Company with no projects: empty state (isEmpty). 403 mid-session: forbidden state distinct from error. COSTING.VIEW absent: route guard blocks.

title: Multi-tenant isolation — company A cannot see company B projects, tasks, timesheets, costs
preconditions: Company A and company B each with projects, tasks, timesheets, and cost postings. User is company-A ORG_ADMIN.
steps:
1. GET /projects?companyId={B} — expect 403 (ScopeGuard.assertCanActIn).
2. GET /projects/uid/{B-project} — expect 403 or not found.
3. POST /project-issues with company-B project uid — expect denied.
4. GET /project-costing/wip?companyId={B} — expect 403.
testData: Company B companyId and project uid
expected: All cross-tenant access denied. Company A only sees its own data. rootadmin can cross tenants (positive control — validates isolation is for non-superusers).

title: RBAC matrix — each PROJECTS action denied when the specific permission is absent
preconditions: Custom roles, one per row, each granted all PROJECTS.* except the one under test.
steps:
1. GET /projects without PROJECTS.PROJECT.VIEW — 403.
2. POST /projects without PROJECTS.PROJECT.CREATE — 403; UI New Project hidden.
3. PUT /projects/uid/{uid} without PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE — 403; save disabled.
4. PATCH .../status without PROJECTS.PROJECT.MANAGE — 403; lifecycle buttons absent.
5. GET /project-tasks/... without PROJECTS.TASK.VIEW — 403; tasks panel hidden.
6. POST /project-tasks/... without PROJECTS.TASK.MANAGE — 403; Add Task hidden.
7. GET /project-timesheets/... without PROJECTS.TIMESHEET.VIEW — 403; panel hidden.
8. POST /project-timesheets/... without PROJECTS.TIMESHEET.RECORD — 403; Record Time hidden.
9. POST /project-issues without PROJECTS.ISSUE.CREATE — 403; Issue Materials hidden.
10. GET /project-costing/.../pnl without PROJECTS.COSTING.VIEW — 403; View P&L hidden.
expected: Each call returns 403. Corresponding UI control is hidden (canCreate, canManage, canTaskManage, canTimesheetRecord, canTimesheetView, canIssue, canCosting). User holding ONLY the required permission succeeds on the guarded endpoint.

title: VIEW-only user — all read panels visible; all mutating controls hidden
preconditions: CUSTOM role = PROJECTS.PROJECT.VIEW + PROJECTS.TASK.VIEW + PROJECTS.TIMESHEET.VIEW + PROJECTS.COSTING.VIEW. A project with tasks and timesheets seeded.
steps:
1. Log in as the VIEW-only user.
2. Navigate to /admin/projects — list visible, New Project button absent.
3. Open the project detail — edit save, lifecycle buttons, Add Task, Record Time, Issue Materials all absent.
4. Verify Tasks, Timesheets, and P&L panels are visible and readable.
5. Verify direct API mutations (PUT, POST, PATCH) all return 403.
expected: All read panels render correctly. Every mutating affordance is absent. Direct API mutations return 403. Axe scan clean on the read-only detail page.

title: Branch scoping — acting in an unassigned branch denied for project create and issue
preconditions: Multi-branch company. User assigned to branch X only. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.CREATE and PROJECTS.ISSUE.CREATE.
steps:
1. Set X-Branch-Uid to branch X (assigned) and POST /projects — succeeds.
2. Set X-Branch-Uid to branch Y (unassigned) and POST /projects — denied.
3. Set X-Branch-Uid to branch Y and POST /project-issues — denied.
expected: Acting in X succeeds. Acting in Y returns denied error (scope guard / branch enforcement). User assigned to ALL branches succeeds in any branch. Default vs non-default assigned branches both work when assigned.

title: Accessibility sweep — project list, detail, and WIP report screens
preconditions: A populated project with tasks, timesheets, and costs. User has PROJECTS.PROJECT.VIEW and PROJECTS.COSTING.VIEW.
steps:
1. Run axe scan on /admin/projects (list).
2. Run axe scan on /admin/projects/uid/:uid (detail).
3. Run axe scan on /admin/projects/wip-report.
4. Keyboard-navigate the list table, paginator, lifecycle buttons, and uid-pickers.
5. Verify tables have captions/scope, pickers and lifecycle buttons have aria-labels.
6. Verify error and empty states are also axe-clean.
expected: Axe-clean WCAG 2.1 AA on all three screens. All controls keyboard-operable. No raw uid visible anywhere on screen (uid only in URL path). Paginator keyboard-operable on list and timesheets panel.
